detail.summary: Foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (decoupling cognition from control) and the deliberate inclusion of dissonance to prevent premature closure on unverified truths. CD-AI frameworks specifically operationalize this doubt.
detail.reason: Revising to integrate CD-AI concepts as a methodology for axiom testing.

detail.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
detail.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
detail.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

children.title: Epistemic Justice and Foundational Assumptions in AI Metareasoning

detail.title: Epistemic Justice and Foundational Assumptions in AI Metareasoning
detail.summary: AI metareasoning frameworks benefit from integrating epistemic justice to recognize community expertise and ethics-based auditing to structure validation of automated outcomes. New evidence suggests that metareasoning processes, particularly when handling model misspecification, are subject to path-dependent inferential errors. Effective augmentation requires maintaining cognitive flow, which necessitates that systems adapt interventions to the user's current contextual state while remaining aware of inherent path-dependency risks in belief updating.
detail.reason: Revision incorporating path-dependency findings from preference research into meta-reasoning frameworks.

detail.title: Metareasoning and Robustness in Rational Agency
detail.summary: Metareasoning-partitioning challenges require optimal resource allocation, while neuro-symbolic frameworks provide mechanisms for detecting and correcting model errors in dynamic environments. detail.reason: Incorporating new evidence on neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks and metacognitive AI into the established metareasoning inquiry.
